questions.text: What is the StressEquilibrium weak form for, and what does the nlgeom parameter do?

keyFacts.fact: fd.weakform.StressEquilibrium(constitutivelaw, incompressibility=None, convert_tangent=True, name='', nlgeom=None, space=None) is the mechanical equilibrium equation for solids, usable for a solid in 3D or using a 2D plane assumption (plane strain or plane stress)

keyFacts.fact: nlgeom: set to False if geometric nonlinearities are ignored; True or 'UL' activates geometric nonlinearities based on the updated Lagrangian method (update the mesh); 'TL' uses the total Lagrangian method (based on the initial mesh with initial displacement effect); if not defined, the problem.nlgeom parameter is used instead (used in the context of NonLinearStatic or NonLinearNewmark problems)

keyFacts.fact: The weak form accepts geometric nonlinearities only if simcoon is installed (nlgeom in {True, 'UL', 'TL'}); in that case the initial displacement is also considered and several corotational formulations may be used by setting the corate attribute (default 'log_r', other options 'log', 'jaumann', 'green_naghdi'/'gn', ...)

questions.text: What does the NLGEOM,ON command do in ANSYS Mechanical APDL?

keyFacts.fact: NLGEOM,Key 'includes large-deflection effects in a static or full transient analysis'; Key=OFF ignores large-deflection effects (a small-deflection analysis is specified) and Key=ON includes large-deflection (large rotation) effects or large strain effects, according to the element type
Command default: large-deflection effects are ignored (NLGEOM,OFF is the default)
When large-deflection effects are included (NLGEOM,ON), stress stiffening effects are also included automatically
If used during the solution (/SOLU), the command is valid only within the first load step; it is also valid in PREP7

questions.text: What is the FKN real constant in penalty contact in ANSYS Mechanical APDL, and what is its default value?

keyFacts.fact: FKN is real constant R3, the 'normal penalty stiffness factor'; the penalty method (KEYOPT(2) = 1) uses the real constants FKN and FKT for all values of KEYOPT(10), plus FTOLN and SLTO if KEYOPT(10) = 0 or 2

keyFacts.fact: FKN defines a normal contact stiffness factor; the usual factor range is from 0.1 to 10.0, with a default of 1.0 (Section 3.9.4.2); a negative value for FKN defines an absolute normal contact stiffness

questions.text: How do I create a ModelingSpace for 2D plane and 3D problems in fedoo?

keyFacts.fact: fd.ModelingSpace(dimension, name='Main') creates the space in which coordinates and variables (functions over coordinates) are defined; a modeling space is required to be able to define weak equations
dimension must be one of '2D', '3D', '2Dplane', '2Dstress', '2Daxi'; the string '2D' is mapped to '2Dplane'

'2D'/'2Dplane' = general 2D problems with default coordinates 'X' and 'Y' and plane strain assumption (ndim=2); '3D' = 3D problems with coordinates 'X', 'Y', 'Z' (ndim=3); '2Dstress' = same as 2D but with plane stress assumption; '2Daxi' = same as 2D but with axisymmetric assumption

keyFacts.fact: A newly created ModelingSpace automatically becomes the active space and is stored in the class dictionary under its name (retrievable as fd.ModelingSpace['Main']); the active space can be changed with make_active() or set_active(name) and read with get_active()

questions.text: In ANSYS Mechanical APDL, how do I set up a nonlinear large-deflection static structural analysis (e.g. a thin plate or a long slender bar in bending)? Which solution control commands should I set for robust convergence - automatic time stepping, line search, Newton-Raphson option, convergence criteria?

keyFacts.fact: NLGEOM,ON activates large-deflection effects; select Large Displacement Static when large deflections are expected (e.g. a long, slender bar under bending)
LNSRCH activates the line search option (listed in the Nonlinear tab options of Solution Controls)
PRED activates a predictor on the degree-of-freedom solution; NEQIT specifies the maximum number of equilibrium iterations allowed per substep
CNVTOL sets the convergence criteria; CUTCONTROL controls bisections (cutback criteria)

NROPT (Newton-Raphson option) is used only in a nonlinear analysis and specifies how often the tangent matrix is updated: Program-chosen (default), Full, Modified, Initial stiffness, Full with unsymmetric matrix
AUTOTS enables automatic time stepping; DELTIM and NSUBST control the time step size / number of substeps (TIME sets time at end of load step)

questions.text: In ANSYS Mechanical APDL, how do I set up surface-to-surface contact between two bodies? Which contact algorithm should I use (penalty, augmented Lagrangian, Lagrange multiplier) and what are the tradeoffs? How do I control the contact stiffness and friction?

keyFacts.fact: KEYOPT(2) on the contact element selects the contact algorithm: 1 = penalty method, 0 = augmented Lagrangian (default), 3 = Lagrange multiplier on contact normal + penalty on tangent, 4 = pure Lagrange multiplier, 2 = internal multipoint constraint (MPC)

The penalty method uses a contact spring whose stiffness is the contact stiffness; it uses real constants FKN (normal contact stiffness factor) and FKT (tangent contact stiffness factor), plus FTOLN and SLTO if KEYOPT(10) = 0 or 2

The augmented Lagrangian method (default) is an iterative series of penalty methods; contact tractions are augmented during equilibrium iterations so final penetration is smaller than the allowable tolerance (FTOLN); it leads to better conditioning and is less sensitive to contact stiffness magnitude but may need more iterations with distorted meshes

The pure Lagrange multiplier method enforces zero penetration when closed and zero slip when sticking; it does not require FKN/FKT but requires chattering control parameters FTOLN and TNOP; it adds contact tractions as additional DOFs and often increases computational cost

FTOLN is the thickness-based factor used to calculate allowable penetration; SLTO controls maximum sliding distance when MU (friction coefficient) is nonzero; PZER defines pressure at zero penetration; CZER defines initial clearance

Lagrange multiplier methods (KEYOPT(2) = 3, 4) introduce zero diagonal terms in the stiffness matrix, so iterative solvers (e.g. PCG) encounter a preconditioning matrix singularity - switch to the sparse solver; also not compatible with Gauss point detection (KEYOPT(4) = 0)

questions.text: How do I model isotropic von Mises (J2) plasticity with hardening in fedoo (the Python FE library) - e.g. a 2D beam in plane strain undergoing plastic bending? Which constitutive law class, weak form, and nonlinear solver do I use, and how is the Newton-Raphson loop driven?

keyFacts.fact: fedoo.constitutivelaw.ElastoPlasticity(young_modulus, poisson_ratio, yield_stress, name='') is a J2 elasto-plastic constitutive law with isotropic hardening (local return mapping, n_statev=7, statev = [P, EP(6)]); hardening is defined via set_hardening_function(function_type, **kwargs)
ElastoPlasticity does NOT implement the plane-stress ('2Dstress') return mapping; for plane-stress models use a Simcoon plasticity law, e.g. fedoo.constitutivelaw.Simcoon("EPICP", props)
fedoo.constitutivelaw.Simcoon("EPICP", props) with props = np.array([E, nu, alpha, Re, k, m]) gives isotropic plasticity with power law hardening sigma = k*eps_p**m

Standard workflow: fd.ModelingSpace("2Dplane"); mesh = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(nx=41, ny=21, x_min=0, x_max=L, y_min=0, y_max=h, elm_type="quad4", name="Domain"); wf = fd.weakform.StressEquilibrium("ConstitutiveLaw", nlgeom=False); fd.Assembly.create(wf, "Domain", "quad4", name="Assembling"); pb = fd.problem.NonLinear("Assembling")

The incremental nonlinear solve is driven by pb.nlsolve(dt=0.05, tmax=1, update_dt=False, tol_nr=0.05, interval_output=0.05), or by a manual Newton-Raphson loop: pb.assembly.set_start(pb), pb.apply_boundary_conditions(t_fact, t_fact_old), pb.set_A(pb.assembly.get_global_matrix()), pb.set_D(pb.assembly.get_global_vector()), pb.solve(), then pb.assembly.update(pb) in sub-iterations until norm_res < tol_nr

Boundary conditions: pb.bc.add("Dirichlet", nodes, "Disp", 0) / pb.bc.add("Dirichlet", nodes, "DispY", uimp); outputs: pb.add_output(path, "Assembling", ["Disp", "Stress", "Strain", "Statev", "Wm"], output_type="Node", file_format="vtk")

questions.text: In fedoo (the Python FE library), how do I define the weak form of mechanical equilibrium for solids (the StressEquilibrium weak form), including geometric nonlinearity and near-incompressibility handling? And how do I create a 2D rectangular mesh with the mesh builders?

keyFacts.fact: fd.weakform.StressEquilibrium(constitutivelaw, incompressibility=None, convert_tangent=True, name="", nlgeom=None, space=None) is the mechanical equilibrium weak form, usable for 3D solids or 2D plane assumptions (plane strain / plane stress)

nlgeom parameter: False = ignore geometric nonlinearities; True or 'UL' = updated Lagrangian method (mesh is updated); 'TL' = total Lagrangian method; if not defined, the problem.nlgeom parameter is used (used in NonLinearStatic / NonLinearNewmark problems)
The incompressibility attribute selects the method used to avoid volumetric locking of nearly incompressible materials; by default (None) the standard displacement formulation is used

The weak form creates the DOF vector "Disp" (DispX, DispY, and DispZ in 3D), tags second-order time evolution, and the corate attribute selects the corotational formulation (default 'log_r', other options 'log', 'jaumann', 'gn'...)
fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(nx=11, ny=11, x_min=0, x_max=1, y_min=0, y_max=1, elm_type='quad4', ndim=None, name='') creates a rectangular mesh; elm_type in {'tri3','tri6','quad4','quad8','quad9'}

Other mesh builders exist: box_mesh (3D volume mesh, simple.py line 478) and disk_mesh(radius, nr, nt, elm_type='quad4') (structured_mesh.py line 408); modeling spaces are set with fd.ModelingSpace("2Dplane") or "3D"

questions.text: In ANSYS Mechanical APDL, how do I set up a nonlinear full transient dynamic analysis (e.g. a structure under a fast time-varying load with large deflections)? Which analysis type command do I use, how do I control the time stepping and the transient integration, and how do I handle initial conditions and results output?

keyFacts.fact: ANTYPE,Antype,Status,LDSTEP,SUBSTEP,Action,--,PRELP specifies the analysis type: 'TRANS or 4' performs a transient analysis (valid for all degrees of freedom); the command default is a new static analysis (Antype defaults to STATIC if none specified)

Two methods are available for transient dynamic analysis: the full method uses the full system matrices (no matrix reduction) and enables all types of nonlinearities (plasticity, large deflections, large strain, and so on); the mode-superposition method does not allow nonlinearities, requires a constant time step throughout the transient (automatic time stepping not allowed) and does not accept imposed (nonzero) displacements
keyFacts.source: C:\Users\connessn\Datas\02_RECHERCHE\00_Biblio\Doc_tech_ANSYS\Main_documentation_ANSYS\ANSYS_Mechanical_APDL_Structural_Analysis_Guide.txt, Sections 5.2, 5.2.1 Full Method and 5.2.2 Mode-Superposition Method, lines 8129-8167

keyFacts.fact: TIMINT,Key,Lab turns on transient effects: Key=OFF means no transient effects (static or steady-state), Key=ON includes transient (mass or inertia) effects; Lab defaults to ALL; the command default is to include transient effects (ON) for ANTYPE,TRANS; transient initial conditions are introduced at the load step having Key=ON (zero initial velocity and acceleration assumed if no previous substeps exist)

Solution Controls Basic tab: select 'Large Displacement Transient' (ANTYPE/NLGEOM) when large deflections or large strains are expected; AUTOTS (time-step optimization, default ON) increases or decreases the integration time step based on the response, with upper and lower limits specified using DELTIM or NSUBST; NSUBST and DELTIM specify the integration time step (smaller value = higher accuracy)
keyFacts.source: C:\Users\connessn\Datas\02_RECHERCHE\00_Biblio\Doc_tech_ANSYS\Main_documentation_ANSYS\ANSYS_Mechanical_APDL_Structural_Analysis_Guide.txt, Section 5.3.3.2 Using the Basic Tab, lines 8318-8337

keyFacts.fact: Solution Controls Transient tab: TIMINT (time-integration on/off), KBC (ramp the load change over the load step or step-apply it), ALPHAD/BETAD (mass/stiffness damping), MIDTOL (midstep criterion), TRNOPT/TINTOPT selects the time-integration method (default is the Newmark method), TINTP defines the integration parameters controlling the nature of the Newmark and HHT time-integration techniques
keyFacts.source: C:\Users\connessn\Datas\02_RECHERCHE\00_Biblio\Doc_tech_ANSYS\Main_documentation_ANSYS\ANSYS_Mechanical_APDL_Structural_Analysis_Guide.txt, Section 5.3.3.3 Using the Transient Tab (Table 5.1 + special considerations), lines 8343-8396

keyFacts.fact: A transient dynamic analysis requires initial displacement, velocity and acceleration (assumed zero if not specified); nonzero initial conditions are set with the IC and ICROTATE commands (the first load steps can be solved with TIMINT,OFF then TIMINT,ON); in a full transient dynamic analysis only the last substep is written to the results file (.rst) by default - set the OUTRES frequency to write all substeps
